rationale:
Today's quota is 1 long-form, 3 Shorts and 1 carousel. I planned it against this week's playbook, the 30-day no-repeat rule and the 14-day rule that bans long-forms on recent Short topics.

**Long-form (L1, Lane A).** I chose Lane A, a title that starts with a phrase people search, over Lane B, the gray-market lane. Every strong Lane B topic was covered as a Short in the last 14 days: compounded vs counterfeit on 10-17, and retatrutide online or death reports on 10-14, 10-16 and 10-19. A Lane B long-form would break the 14-day ban. There's no fresh 48-hour news for Lane C, and the retatrutide type 2 diabetes trial is too close to yesterday's retatrutide long-form.

"How Long Does Tirzepatide Take to Work?" is one of the playbook's own Lane A examples. It's evergreen and well documented by peer-reviewed trials (weight curves in SURMOUNT-1, blood sugar in SURPASS), and we haven't covered it. It doesn't repeat any recent Short, it isn't a single-trial deep dive or a "Did X beat Y?" frame, and the title is under 60 characters. It must not include any dosing or titration instructions.

**Shorts:**
- **S1 (13:00, lead).** The compounded tirzepatide recall in the gray-market "what's confirmed?" frame, our strongest lane. It's rising news that belongs in a Short, and the recall is a fact we haven't published. It's YouTube-first because gray-market topics barely reach anyone on Instagram.
- **S2 (08:00).** The required spin-off of today's long-form: a named-drug question with "tirzepatide" in the title, framed as a myth correction. I skipped muscle and SURMOUNT-5 head-to-heads because we've covered them repeatedly in the last 30 days, and SURMOUNT-5 already appeared in Shorts on 10-17 and 10-19.
- **S3 (20:00, funnel).** The new retatrutide type 2 diabetes trial (TRANSCEND-T2D-1, rising, momentum 80). It's a spin-off of yesterday's published retatrutide long-form, so it can link to it. I dropped the "approved yet?" framing, which is banned.

**Carousel (C1).** Minimum effort, as the playbook says: it reuses the verified text from the 10-15 diabetic eye disease Short, with no new research. It also covers a different body system from the other pieces.

**Mix:** about 40% rising (S1, S3), 40% evergreen with a timely hook (L1, C1) and 20% myth correction (S2).

**Pillars:** results, is-it-for-you, myths, research and beyond-weight, so no pillar is used twice.

**Topics skipped:**
- I treated the recall (caution) with an evidence-first angle and did not use the other caution items: PCOS, copay and surgery.
- The muscle, side-effect discontinuation, sleep apnea, orforglipron ACHIEVE-4 and stopping/SURMOUNT-4 topics repeat angles we covered in the last 30 days.

pieces.topic: How long tirzepatide takes to work: a timeline of appetite, blood sugar, weight and blood pressure based on the published randomized trials (SURMOUNT-1 in adults with obesity, or overweight plus a weight-related condition, without diabetes, 72 weeks; SURPASS trials in type 2 diabetes)
pieces.angle: How long tirzepatide takes to work, measure by measure. Weight (SURMOUNT-1: adults with obesity, or overweight plus a weight-related condition, without diabetes, 72 weeks): use only the numbers the NEJM paper reports, or figures read approximately from its graph and labelled 'about'. Give per-arm group sizes and the estimand. Blood sugar (SURPASS, type 2 diabetes only): HbA1c at the reported timepoints. Blood pressure: only at the timepoints the trials reported (SURMOUNT-1, week 72). Appetite: explained as mechanism, with no week-by-week claims unless a named human study measured it. Say the trials raised the dose gradually by design, with no numbers. 'Averages, not predictions.' Plateau and slower responders. Common GI side effects are most frequent early on, plus habits with their caveats. Don't change, stop or switch on your own. CTA: an already-published Lane A or Life on GLP-1 long-form, not 'Did Retatrutide Beat Tirzepatide?'. Prescriber line.
pieces.working_title: How Long Does Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) Take to Work?
pieces.target_keyword: how long does tirzepatide take to work
pieces.why: A Lane A search-question title the playbook names itself. People search it constantly, it rests on peer-reviewed RCT data, and it doesn't repeat any Short from the last 14 days. | fact-check: Good Lane A search topic with an evergreen question and solid trial data (SURMOUNT-1 in NEJM 2022, the SURPASS program). Three changes are needed. (1) Appetite chapter: SURMOUNT-1 did not measure a timeline of appetite or 'food noise'. Don't give an appetite timeline unless the script cites a specific published human study that measured appetite or energy intake at named weeks. If no such study is cited, present appetite as how the drug works, with no week claims. (2) Blood pressure: only use timepoints the trials actually reported (SURMOUNT-1's main BP result is change at week 72). Don't make up an early-weeks BP timeline. (3) Weight at month 3, 6 and 12: read off the published figure, these are approximations. Say 'about' and 'read from the trial's published graph', or use only time points the paper reports in numbers. Keep the per-arm group sizes, the estimand and 'averages, not predictions'. Explain plainly that early results partly reflect the trial's built-in gradual dose increase, with no numbers or schedules. CTA problem: the playbook flags 'Did Retatrutide Beat Tirzepatide?' as a banned frame with no head-to-head trial behind it, and it's in a different lane. Sending Lane A viewers there undermines the experiment and points them to an indirect comparison. Name an already-published Lane A or 'Life on GLP-1' long-form instead. If none exists, use the end screen plus 'follow the Life on GLP-1 series'. Keep the GI side-effects line, the fluids caveat ('unless you've been told to limit fluids'), the protein caveat (check first if you have kidney disease), 'don't change, stop or switch on your own' and the prescriber line. Title: 'How Long Does Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) Take to Work?' is 51 characters with no numbers or abbreviations, so it's OK.

pieces.topic: Compounded tirzepatide recall: Houston RX recalled 64 vials (Class II, lack of sterility assurance, started Sep 25, 2026) after an FDA inspection with 14 observations
pieces.angle: Calm 'what's confirmed?' Short. Per the FDA enforcement report (cite the entry and its report date), Houston RX LLC, a Texas compounding pharmacy, recalled 64 vials of compounded tirzepatide-niacinamide, Class II, for lack of assurance of sterility, initiated Sep 25, 2026 (confirm against the FDA record). An FDA inspection on Aug 20–28, 2026 listed 14 observations (FDA Form 483). One line: anything injected has to be sterile. Compounded drugs aren't FDA-approved or reviewed; branded tirzepatide is FDA-approved. Ask your prescriber or pharmacist what product you're on and about FDA-approved options. Don't switch, stop or change your medicines on your own. Prescriber line. Follow for more. No emoji, 170 words or fewer.
pieces.working_title: Compounded Tirzepatide Recall: What the FDA Confirmed (Oct 2026) #shorts
pieces.why: Our strongest Short lane (gray-market 'what's confirmed?' Shorts: median 103.5) with a new fact: mainstream recall coverage peaked on Oct 19. | fact-check: Mostly confirmed. FDA enforcement-report data relayed by Medical Daily and others: Houston RX LLC (a 503A pharmacy) recalled 64 vials, Class II, for lack of assurance of sterility, initiated Sep 25, 2026. The FDA Form 483 (fda.gov/media/195122) covers an inspection on Aug 20–28, 2026 with 14 observations. Corrections and risks: (1) The recalled product is compounded tirzepatide-NIACINAMIDE 20 mg/2 mg per mL vials, not plain tirzepatide. The title and narration must say 'compounded tirzepatide-niacinamide vials' or 'a compounded tirzepatide combination', or the claim is wrong. (2) One secondary site gives the initiation date as Sep 10. The scriptwriter must confirm the date, class, quantity and reason against the FDA Enforcement Report entry itself and cite that entry with its report date. If the entry can't be retrieved, cite only the 483 and leave out the date. (3) Keep to what was confirmed: one pharmacy and 64 vials. The FDA has not reported injuries in the sources found, so don't imply harm or widespread contamination, and don't list graphic or alarming 483 details (exposed skin, microbial growth) beyond one calm line. Naming the recalling firm, credited to the FDA record, is acceptable. Name no other pharmacy, telehealth or seller. (4) Say compounded drugs are not FDA-approved and not FDA-reviewed for safety, effectiveness or quality, and that branded tirzepatide (Mounjaro, Zepbound) is FDA-approved, without making it sound like an ad. Title: drop dosing details. 'Compounded Tirzepatide Recall: What the FDA Confirmed (Oct 2026)' is fine if the body says 'tirzepatide-niacinamide'.

pieces.topic: Tirzepatide not working yet? Why trial weight loss built gradually over months rather than weeks
pieces.angle: Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) not working yet? In SURMOUNT-1 (adults with obesity, or overweight plus a weight-related condition, without diabetes), average weight loss built over months, not weeks, and kept going late into the 72 weeks. Use one exactly copied NEJM figure with dose arm, n per arm, placebo comparator, estimand and timepoint. One line: the trial raised the dose gradually by design, and your prescriber decides yours, never adjust it yourself. Averages, not predictions. One GI side-effects line. Don't change, stop or switch on your own; ask your prescriber about your progress. Prescriber line. Run it the day after L1 publishes, with the L1 'Full breakdown' CTA.
pieces.working_title: Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) Not Working Yet? What the Trial Shows #shorts
pieces.why: Spin-off of L1 that sends viewers to today's long-form. It names the drug ('tirzepatide' titles: median 83) and makes a myth-busting point that's true. | fact-check: Good myth correction, and SURMOUNT-1 supports it: weight loss built over months and was still going at the later timepoints. Risk: a 'not working yet?' frame can push frustrated viewers toward raising the dose themselves, microdosing or gray-market products. The Short must say plainly that the trial's gradual dose increase was part of the design and is set by the prescriber, with no numbers or schedule. Use one number exactly as printed in NEJM (e.g. mean % change at week 72 for one named dose vs placebo, with that arm's n and the placebo n, and the estimand), or an earlier timepoint only if the paper reports it in numbers. Don't add an early-weeks number read off the graph. The title has no number, OK. Scheduling: the playbook says funnel Shorts run the day after their long-form. Publish S2 after L1 is live so the 'Full breakdown' CTA is valid. If it runs before, end on 'follow for more' as specified. Keep 'averages, not predictions', one GI line, 'don't change, stop or switch on your own; ask your prescriber about your progress' and the prescriber line.

pieces.topic: Retatrutide in type 2 diabetes: the first Phase 3 diabetes trial, TRANSCEND-T2D-1 (537 adults whose type 2 diabetes was managed with diet and exercise, 40 weeks, vs placebo, The Lancet)
pieces.angle: Retatrutide in type 2 diabetes: TRANSCEND-T2D-1 (The Lancet, 2026), 40 weeks vs placebo, adults whose type 2 diabetes wasn't controlled with diet and exercise alone. One weight number for the top dose vs placebo with per-arm n and the named estimand, then one HbA1c line with its arm and the placebo figure. Placebo-controlled only, no tirzepatide arm. Status, credited to Lilly with a date: investigational, not FDA-approved as of Oct 2026; Lilly plans to file in Q1 2027, and a plan to file isn't approval. One GI line. No online products. Ask a prescriber about approved options or clinical trials. Prescriber line. CTA to 'Did Retatrutide Beat Tirzepatide?' only if that video is published and says the comparison is indirect; otherwise 'follow for more'.
pieces.working_title: Retatrutide in Type 2 Diabetes: How Much Weight in 40 Weeks? #shorts
pieces.why: Spin-off of yesterday's live retatrutide long-form, sending traffic to it. It's a new trial we haven't covered, and retatrutide searches are up (radar momentum 80). | fact-check: Confirmed: TRANSCEND-T2D-1 was a 40-week, randomized, double-blind trial of retatrutide vs placebo in 537 adults whose type 2 diabetes was inadequately controlled with diet and exercise (HbA1c 7.0–9.5%, BMI ≥23), published in The Lancet and presented at ADA in June 2026. Reported weight change: 4 mg −11.5%, 9 mg −13.9%, 12 mg −15.3%, placebo −2.6%. Lilly also reported −16.8% for 12 mg under a different estimand, and the two get mixed up. The script must name the estimand next to the number it uses and use per-arm n from the Lancet paper, not 537. Status: Lilly said (Jul 2026) it plans to submit to the FDA in Q1 2027. The status line must be credited to a Lilly statement dated at or near that date, not to the June trial paper. Population wording: 'type 2 diabetes managed with diet and exercise alone, not well controlled'. These were not people with obesity specifically (BMI ≥23). CTA problem: the playbook says 'Did Retatrutide Beat Tirzepatide?' uses a frame with no randomized head-to-head trial behind it, and this Short states correctly that there was no tirzepatide arm. Funnelling viewers into a 'beat' title right after saying so is contradictory. Point the CTA there only if that video is published and clearly calls its comparison indirect. Otherwise use 'follow for more' and a related-video link to another published retatrutide long-form. This is a single-drug Short in the weak 20:00 slot, which is acceptable as a test.
